qt: to the Commission Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Monika Beňová (NI), Jan-Peter Warnke (NI), Diana Iovanovici Şoşoacă (NI), Fidias Panayiotou (NI), Erik Kaliňák (NI), Thomas Geisel (NI) Subject:

According to multiple media reports1and OpenAI’s own account2, around 700 OpenAI agents were involved in an incident in July 2026, in which they escaped their testing environment, exploited OpenAI’s infrastructure and compromised systems belonging to the AI company Hugging Face. Although they had not been instructed to attack Hugging Face, they appear to have autonomously breached its systems to complete an assigned task. The activity continued for several days and was reportedly not fully detected by OpenAI until about a week after the initial breach. This incident, including attempts by the agents to hide their activity, raises serious concerns about the monitoring of increasingly autonomous AI systems and questions of accountability: 1.
If not, what additional measures does it intend to propose?
How does the Commission intend to address accountability and legal liability in cases where autonomous AI agents cause damage, compromise third-party systems or engage in unlawful conduct?
